sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Wildwood, MO?
sections.html:
Wildwood covers about 67 square miles at the western edge of St. Louis County. A seller here deals with St. Louis County for building records, inspections and tax bills, and with the city itself for zoning and, in the case of rentals, occupancy permits. Owner-occupied sales do not need an occupancy permit.

The Census Bureau estimates 34,955 residents for July 1, 2025, compared with 35,417 counted in 2020. The 2020 density was 531.5 people per square mile, against 5,967.5 in University City, so lot size and distance from neighbors are a bigger part of the picture here.

sections.h2: Where is Wildwood and how did it become a city?
sections.html:
Wildwood is in the far western part of St. Louis County. It was incorporated on September 1, 1995. It covers 67.08 square miles, including 0.66 square miles of water. Chesterfield is to the north, Clarkson Valley and Ellisville to the east, Eureka and Pacific to the south, and Franklin County to the west.

Parks shape the area. The Al Foster Trail runs through the city, and Rockwoods Reservation and Babler State Park are nearby. The Big Chief Restaurant is what remains of a tourist complex that opened on U.S. Route 66 in 1928, and the National Register of Historic Places listed it in 2003.

Most of Wildwood belongs to the Rockwood School District, and Lafayette High School is within the city limits. A small part lies in the Meramec Valley School District. St. Louis Community College has a Wildwood campus off Routes 100 and 109. The city contracts with the St. Louis County Police Department for police service.

sections.h2: How do Wildwood homes compare with other places in Missouri?
sections.html:
Wildwood has the highest home values and incomes of the four Missouri places in this set of guides, and the highest share of owner-occupied homes.

With 91.8 percent of homes owner-occupied, rentals are rare, and a typical buyer plans to live in the house. The median age was 44.1 at the 2020 census, and 73.4 percent of households were married-couple households.

The 2020 census counted 12,481 households and 12,918 housing units in Wildwood, and only 3.4 percent of those units were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.1 percent. Residents 65 and older make up 20.7 percent of the population, a group likely to include owners thinking about a move.

sections.h2: Does Wildwood require an occupancy permit to sell a house?
sections.html:
Not for an owner-occupied sale. Wildwood's residential occupancy permit applies only to non-owner-occupied homes, and the city's program lists an effective date of March 1, 2025. An occupancy permit and inspection are required when the occupant of a rental or other non-owner-occupied house changes, and new construction or owner-occupied homes do not need an inspection or permit.

  • The inspection is performed by St. Louis County Public Works, and a passed inspection is not a permit by itself.
  • The city's permit fee is $40, or $20 to update occupants, and the application can go through the city's MyGov portal.
  • The inspection fee covers the first visit and a second one; each extra visit costs $50.
  • The application lapses after 90 days if noted deficiencies are not corrected.
  • Belongings should be out of the home at the time of inspection.

This matters when you sell to an investor who plans to rent the house, because the new tenant cannot move in until the permit is issued. Metro West Fire Protection District also requires its own inspection within its service area, while the city's page says the Eureka and Monarch districts do not require one for single-family homes. Confirm with your fire district, since that can change.

sections.h2: What permits and city rules affect a Wildwood property?
sections.html:
If a buyer or seller wants to change the house before closing, the city's Planning Department at 16860 Main Street, phone 636-458-0440, handles zoning authorization. Fences, decks, sheds, pools and retaining walls all need at least zoning authorization. Building permits follow the St. Louis County building code, and the county Public Works office takes calls at 314-615-2559.

  • A building permit is required for additions, new construction, electrical or mechanical work, new or replaced plumbing, structural alterations, above-ground pools and certain retaining walls.
  • Sheds of 120 square feet or less and fences under six feet do not need a building permit, but still need zoning authorization.
  • Grass over 10 inches is a nuisance under the city's code enforcement rules.
  • Trash containers must be kept out of view from the street in front of the house.

Utilities vary by address: Missouri American Water supplies water, MSD Project Clear provides sewer service, and trash is collected by Republic Services in urban areas or Gateway Disposal on rural and private roads. Residents 65 and older can get a 15 percent trash discount by contacting the hauler. Tell your buyer which hauler serves the address.

sections.h2: How are Wildwood property taxes handled when I sell?
sections.html:
All property taxes for Wildwood are managed by St. Louis County. Taxes must be paid or postmarked by December 31 of the billing year, and later payments carry interest of up to 18 percent a year plus a 2 percent penalty under RSMo chapters 139 and 140, as the county Collector states. The Collector's office is in Clayton at 41 S. Central Avenue; call (314) 615-7100, or (314) 615-7865 for back taxes.

The County Assessor reassesses all real estate in odd-numbered years, so the next full reassessment falls in 2027. The Board of Equalization takes appeals from May 1 to the second Monday in July. The 2026 date of July 13 has passed. Ask your title company for a payoff figure before you set a closing date, since a delinquent balance is paid from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Wildwood house?
sections.html:
Some owners need a quick sale because of a move, an estate or repairs, and others have time to prepare. Here are the common paths.

  • List with an agent. Ask about the commission and the cost of any repairs a buyer's inspector will raise.
  • Sell by owner. You keep control of price and showings but handle contracts and disclosures.
  • Sell to an investor. An investor may buy as is and close on a date you choose. Compare the written offer with your likely net from a listing.

Before you list, find out who maintains your road. The city's FAQ says a street may belong to Wildwood, St. Louis County, MoDOT or another municipality, and the Public Works office will help you find the right contact.

faqs.q: Does Wildwood require an occupancy permit when I sell my home?
faqs.a: No, not for an owner-occupied home. The permit applies to non-owner-occupied properties when the occupant changes, and the program's effective date was March 1, 2025.

faqs.q: How much is the Wildwood residential occupancy permit?
faqs.a: The city fee is $40, or $20 to update occupants. The inspection through St. Louis County is separate, and each visit after the second costs $50.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill for a house in Wildwood?
faqs.a: St. Louis County does. The Collector of Revenue is at 41 S. Central Avenue in Clayton, and taxes are due by December 31 each year.
Most of the city is in the Rockwood School District, and Lafayette High School is inside city limits. A small part is in the Meramec Valley School District.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Wildwood?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $495,800 for owner-occupied homes for 2020 to 2024, with 91.8 percent of homes owner-occupied and a median household income of $161,060.
